newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Placer cleaning up Philippine river.
newsitem.headline: Placer cleaning up Philippine river.

text.p: Canada's Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday it would spend $70-75 million to clean up a river polluted by tailings from a copper mine it used to be part-owner of in the Philippines.
In March, Placer pulled out of Marcopper Mining Corp, in which it had a 39.9 percent stake.
Marcopper's copper mine in the island of Marinduque had already been closed for a year after a serious leak of tailings into the Boac River.

Placer President, John Willson, told reporters the company had already spent $40 million on the clean-up and $800,000 to compensate local people affected by the damage. The money will come from insurance.

"We hope to push the tailings into a trench as soon as the rain comes (around July)" Willson said. Between 25 and 30 percent of the tailings were still in the river and clean-up work would continue up to next year, he added.
The leak in the tunnel of the mine was estimated to have dumped 1.5 million cubic metres of tailings or mine wastes, and affected wide stretches of the 25 km (15.5 mile) long Boac river.
The government later filed criminal charges against two Placer executives at Marcopper for the accident.
Despite its experience in Marcopper, Placer has applied for three gold prospects in the country, two on the island of Luzon and the other in Mindanao.
It will spend $1 million on exploration in the Philippines this year and about $120 million worldwide, Willson said.
"We are exploring (for new mines in the Philippines). If we find something ... we will invest," he added.
